name: get_interface_state
description: Get a structured snapshot of the current NimbusImage interface state: dataset, collection, location (XY/Z/Time), layer mode, camera, layers (id, name, channel, color, contrast, visibility), selected tool, active annotation filters, and annotation counts. Cheap and precise — prefer this over capture_screenshot for questions about application state. Read-only.

name: capture_screenshot
description: Capture a screenshot and receive it as an image. 'viewport' shows just the rendered image in the viewer (reliable), 'interface' shows the whole application window (may miss some WebGL content). Use only when you need to see image content (e.g. what kind of cells are visible); use get_interface_state for application state. Read-only.

target.description: Which screenshot(s) to capture. Default: viewport.

name: get_annotation_summary
description: Get annotation counts grouped by tag, shape and channel, plus the count of currently filtered and selected annotations. Read-only.

name: list_annotations
description: List annotations matching a query, with id, name, shape, tags, channel, location, color and centroid. Use this to inspect specific annotations, not to enumerate a whole dataset: for counts or a breakdown by tag/shape/channel, prefer get_annotation_summary. Results are paged (default 50, max 200); the result reports totalMatching, hasMore and nextOffset, so page further only when you need those specific items. Read-only.

query.description: Filter for annotations. All given conditions must match. Omit all fields to match every annotation.

tags.description: Annotations having at least one of these tags (or all, if exclusive is true).

exclusive.description: If true, annotations must have ALL the given tags.

currentFrameOnly.description: Only annotations at the current XY/Z/Time location.

limit.description: Maximum number of annotations to return (default 50, hard-capped at 200). For larger match sets, page with offset or call get_annotation_summary for counts and breakdowns instead of listing them all.

name: list_tools
description: List the tools in the current collection's toolset (id, name, type, and the worker image for worker-based tools). Read-only.

name: list_workers
description: List the available worker images (automated annotation algorithms such as Cellpose-SAM or Piscis) with their names and descriptions. Read-only.

name: get_worker_interface
description: Get the parameter schema for a worker image: each parameter's name, type, default, and min/max, plus a `valueFormats` guide describing the exact value shape each type expects and a `channels` list giving the dataset's channel index↔name mapping. Call before run_worker or create_tool to know which workerInterfaceValues can be set and how to format them (channels are 0-based indices; channelCheckboxes slots take an array of indices like [0], not a map). May take a few seconds if the interface is not cached. Read-only.

image.description: The worker Docker image, as returned by list_workers or list_tools.

name: set_location
description: Move the viewer to a different XY position, Z slice and/or time point. Omitted fields keep their current value. Values are clamped to the dataset's range. Visible immediately; reversible.

name: set_camera
description: Pan and/or zoom the viewer camera. Either provide center (image pixel coordinates) and/or zoom (GeoJS zoom level; +1 doubles magnification), OR provide fit to frame the view: 'annotations' (all annotations), 'selection' (the selected ones), or 'full' (the whole image). Visible immediately; reversible.

fit.description: Zoom/pan to frame these; ignores center/zoom if set.

name: set_layer_mode
description: Switch the layer display mode: 'single' (one layer at a time), 'multiple' (blended layers), or 'unroll' (grid of frames; optionally choose which dimensions to unroll). Visible immediately; reversible.

name: update_layer
description: Change one display layer: color (hex), visibility, contrast (black/white points), or name. Color, visibility and name change the shared collection; contrast defaults to the user's personal view override (like the contrast slider), or set contrastScope to 'configuration' to change the shared collection. Refer to the layer by its id or its exact name from get_interface_state. Visible immediately; reversible.

contrastScope.description: Where to save contrast: 'view' (personal, default) or 'configuration' (shared collection).

name: set_layer_visibility
description: Declaratively set which layers are visible: the listed layers (by id or name) become visible, all others are hidden. In 'single' layer mode only pass one layer. Visible immediately; reversible.

visibleLayers.description: Layer ids or names that should be visible.

name: set_display_options
description: Change viewer display options. Provide any subset: drawAnnotations (show/hide annotation overlays), annotationOpacity (0-1), showScalebar, scalebarColor (hex), backgroundColor (hex or name), drawAnnotationConnections. Visible immediately; reversible.

backgroundColor.description: Hex color or CSS color name.

name: set_view_mode
description: Switch the viewer between 2D and 3D (volume) rendering. Visible immediately; reversible.

name: set_scale
description: Set the dataset's physical scale in the collection so measurements use real units. Provide any of pixelSize / zStep (length units: nm, µm, mm, m) and tStep (time units: ms, s, m, h, d). Applies to the shared collection.

name: select_annotations
description: Change the current annotation selection using a query (same query shape as list_annotations). Mode 'replace' sets the selection, 'add' extends it, 'remove' subtracts from it, 'clear' empties it. Reversible.

query.description: Filter for annotations. All given conditions must match. Omit all fields to match every annotation.

tags.description: Annotations having at least one of these tags (or all, if exclusive is true).

exclusive.description: If true, annotations must have ALL the given tags.

currentFrameOnly.description: Only annotations at the current XY/Z/Time location.

name: color_annotations
description: Set the display color of annotations, either the current selection (target 'selection') or those matching a query. Pass color null to clear the override so annotations fall back to their layer color. This edits stored annotations; undoable with the undo tool.

oneOf.description: Filter for annotations. All given conditions must match. Omit all fields to match every annotation.

tags.description: Annotations having at least one of these tags (or all, if exclusive is true).

exclusive.description: If true, annotations must have ALL the given tags.

currentFrameOnly.description: Only annotations at the current XY/Z/Time location.

color.description: Hex color like #RRGGBB, or null to clear.

randomize.description: Give each annotation a random color instead.

name: color_annotations_by_property
description: Color EVERY annotation in the dataset by a computed property value (server-side): numeric values get a colormap ramp, non-numeric values get a categorical palette (see mode for numeric labels like cluster IDs), and a legend explaining the mapping appears in the viewer and persists with the collection. Pass clear true to remove the property coloring (colors fall back to layer colors); clearing is refused as a no-op when no property coloring is active, since it would reset manual colors too. Replaces all existing annotation colors and is NOT undoable; gated, so the user approves first. Ramps default to the 1st-99th percentile of the values so outliers don't collapse the ramp; override with rangeMin/rangeMax or percentileLow/percentileHigh. Any later manual color assignment (color_annotations, or the user coloring by hand) retires the legend. Annotations created after the apply and re-computed values do not re-color automatically; re-apply to refresh.

propertyPath.description: Full property value path from get_property_values (e.g. a nested path like [propertyId, 'Mean', 'Ch1']). Required unless clear is true.

clear.description: Remove the property-based coloring and legend instead of applying one.

mode.description: How to map values to colors. Default 'auto' picks continuous whenever at least 90% of the values are numeric, REGARDLESS of how many distinct values there are — so integer-coded labels like cluster IDs get a misleading gradient under auto. Pass 'categorical' explicitly for numeric labels/IDs; 'continuous' forces a ramp.

colormap.description: Continuous colormap name (e.g. 'viridis'). Omit for the server default; an unknown name fails with the list of valid ones.

rangeMin.description: Absolute lower bound of the ramp; overrides percentileLow.

rangeMax.description: Absolute upper bound of the ramp; overrides percentileHigh.

percentileLow.description: Lower percentile bound of the ramp (default 1).

percentileHigh.description: Upper percentile bound of the ramp (default 99).

name: tag_annotations
description: Add, remove or replace tags on annotations (current selection or a query). This edits stored annotations; undoable with the undo tool.

oneOf.description: Filter for annotations. All given conditions must match. Omit all fields to match every annotation.

tags.description: Annotations having at least one of these tags (or all, if exclusive is true).

exclusive.description: If true, annotations must have ALL the given tags.

currentFrameOnly.description: Only annotations at the current XY/Z/Time location.

name: set_annotation_filter
description: Configure which annotations are shown in the viewer and annotation browser: filter by tags, restrict to the current frame, and/or filter by computed property value ranges (e.g. 'area > 100'). Use clearAll to remove all filters, or clearPropertyFilters for just the property ones. Visible immediately; reversible.

tags.description: Show only annotations with at least one of these tags (all, if exclusive).

propertyFilters.description: Keep only annotations whose property value is within [min, max]. Use the propertyPath from get_property_values.

propertyPath.description: Full property value path from get_property_values.

clearAll.description: Disable the tag filter, current-frame restriction, and property filters.

name: select_tool
description: Activate a tool from the toolset by its id (from list_tools), or pass null to deactivate the current tool. Reversible.

name: create_tool
description: Add a new annotation tool to the current collection's toolset (e.g. 'set up a DAPI blob tool'). Provide EITHER manualShape for a hand-drawing tool OR workerImage for an automated worker tool (from list_workers), not both. ALWAYS provide tags: annotations the tool creates carry these tags, and tags are how annotations are filtered, measured and analyzed downstream — an untagged tool produces annotations that are hard to work with. For a worker tool, FIRST call get_worker_interface for the image and pass workerInterfaceValues: the values are saved with the tool (used when it is run from the UI, pipelines, or run_worker), and unset parameters fall back to defaults that are often wrong for the dataset. Optionally bind it to a channel with channelName and give it a name. Gated: the user approves before the tool is created. The tool is added but NOT activated; use select_tool to make it active, or run_worker to run a worker tool.

manualShape.description: For a manual hand-drawing tool: the annotation shape. 'polygon' is a blob outline.

workerImage.description: For an automated worker tool: the worker Docker image, as returned by list_workers.

channelName.description: Bind the tool to this channel, matching one of the dataset's channel names.

name.description: Optional custom tool name; a channel-prefixed default (e.g. 'DAPI Blob') is used otherwise.

tags.description: Tags applied to every annotation the tool creates (e.g. ["nucleus"]). Always provide at least one tag describing what the tool annotates.

workerInterfaceValues.description: For worker tools only: parameter values keyed by parameter name, saved with the tool (call get_worker_interface first for the schema, valueFormats and channels list). Set every required parameter and any channel/select parameter — their built-in defaults (channel 0, empty selection) are usually wrong for the dataset. Format values per valueFormats: a channel parameter takes a 0-based channel index number; a channelCheckboxes 'slot' takes an array of channel indices to select, e.g. [0] (NOT a map like {"0": 0}, which selects nothing); a select takes one of its items. Anything omitted uses the interface default.

name: list_properties
description: List the annotation property definitions (measurements) set up in this collection, with id, name, worker image, the annotation shape they apply to, tags, and whether they have been computed. Read-only. Use to find a property id to compute or read, and to avoid creating duplicates.

name: create_property
description: Define a new annotation property (measurement) computed by a property worker (e.g. intensity, morphology). Pass propertyWorkerImage (a worker from list_workers whose isPropertyWorker is true) and the annotation shape it applies to; optionally restrict to tags, set worker parameters (get_worker_interface shows them), and name it. Gated: the user approves. This only defines the property — call compute_property to actually compute values.

propertyWorkerImage.description: The property-worker Docker image (from list_workers, isPropertyWorker true).

shape.description: The annotation shape this property applies to.

tags.description: Only apply to annotations having these tags. Omit for all.

exclusive.description: If true, annotations must have ALL the given tags.

name.description: Optional property name; the worker's name is used otherwise.

workerInterfaceValues.description: Worker parameter overrides, formatted per get_worker_interface's valueFormats (channel = 0-based index number; channelCheckboxes slot = array of indices like [0]; select = one of its items); defaults are used for anything omitted.

name: compute_property
description: Compute an existing property definition's values for this dataset's annotations. Pass the propertyId (from list_properties or create_property). Gated: the user approves. Starts a background job; values populate as it runs — read them with get_property_values.

propertyId.description: The id of the property to compute (from list_properties/create_property).

name: get_property_values
description: Read computed property values as summary statistics (count, mean, std, min, max, median, p25, p75) per property value path — not a per-annotation dump. Optionally restrict to one propertyId and/or filter the annotations with a query (same shape as list_annotations). Read-only. Use to answer questions like 'what's the mean intensity of my nuclei?'.

propertyId.description: Restrict to a single property (from list_properties). Omit for all computed properties.

query.description: Annotation filter (same fields as list_annotations' query): only summarize values for matching annotations.

name: get_property_histogram
description: Get a binned histogram (min, max, count per bucket) for one numeric property value path across annotations, optionally restricted by a query (same shape as list_annotations). Use this to inspect the distribution shape (skew, modality, outliers) of a property before deciding what to plot or conclude. Read-only.

propertyPath.description: Property value path segments, as returned by get_property_values' propertyPath.

query.description: Annotation filter (same fields as list_annotations' query).

name: get_sample_values
description: Get up to n sample rows (annotation id, tags, plus the value for each requested property path) so you can eyeball raw data before drawing conclusions. Rows are sampled evenly across the dataset, not the first n. Read-only; default 20 rows, max 100.

propertyPaths.description: Property value paths (each an array of segments).

query.description: Annotation filter (same fields as list_annotations' query).

name: create_scatter_plot
description: Create an interactive scatter plot of one property against another, rendered inline in the panel. Annotations missing a numeric value on either axis are dropped. Optionally color points by each annotation's first tag, and/or restrict annotations with a query (same shape as list_annotations). The raw points are never sent back to you — they render directly for the user; you receive only a plotId and point count. Refer to the plot by its title in your reply.

xPropertyPath.description: Property value path for the x axis (from get_property_values' propertyPath).

yPropertyPath.description: Property value path for the y axis (from get_property_values' propertyPath).

xLabel.description: Optional x-axis label; defaults to the property's full name.

yLabel.description: Optional y-axis label; defaults to the property's full name.

colorByTag.description: One trace per first-tag (untagged grouped together).

query.description: Annotation filter (same fields as list_annotations' query).

name: create_histogram_plot
description: Create an interactive histogram of one numeric property value path, rendered inline in the panel as a bar chart, optionally restricted by a query (same shape as list_annotations). The binned data renders directly for the user and is never sent back to you; you receive only a plotId and bucket count. Refer to the plot by its title in your reply.

propertyPath.description: Property value path segments, as returned by get_property_values' propertyPath.

xLabel.description: Optional x-axis label; defaults to the property's full name.

query.description: Annotation filter (same fields as list_annotations' query).

name: create_box_plot
description: Create an interactive box plot of one or more numeric property value paths, rendered inline in the panel, optionally restricted by a query (same shape as list_annotations). With groupByTag (valid only for a single path) it draws one box per annotation first-tag; otherwise one box per property path. The raw values render directly for the user and are never sent back to you; you receive only a plotId and trace count. Refer to the plot by its title in your reply.

propertyPaths.description: Property value paths (each an array of segments, from get_property_values' propertyPath).

groupByTag.description: One box per annotation first-tag; requires exactly one propertyPath.

query.description: Annotation filter (same fields as list_annotations' query).

name: undo
description: Undo the most recent annotation change in this dataset (create/edit/delete/tag/color). Does not affect view state such as camera or layer settings.

name: redo
description: Redo the most recently undone annotation change in this dataset.

name: run_worker
description: Run a worker-based annotation tool from the toolset (by tool id from list_tools). Starts a compute job that may create many annotations and take minutes; the user must approve. Returns the job id immediately; progress is shown to the user. Optionally override worker parameters (see get_worker_interface for the schema; unspecified parameters use saved or default values).

workerInterfaceValues.description: Parameter overrides keyed by parameter name, formatted per get_worker_interface's valueFormats (channel = 0-based index number; channelCheckboxes slot = array of indices like [0]; select = one of its items). Unspecified parameters use the tool's saved value or the interface default.

name: wait_for_job
description: Block until a background job started by run_worker or compute_property finishes, then report its outcome. This is how you wait for a worker: it returns as soon as the job completes (it listens for the completion event, it does not poll), so one call covers a run of any length. Never check on a job by re-reading state (get_interface_state / get_annotation_summary / get_property_values) in a loop — that burns your turns and you will run out before the job is done. If the wait budget runs out before the job finishes, the result says stillRunning and you may call this again with the same jobId, or tell the user it is still going. Read-only.

jobId.description: The jobId returned by run_worker or compute_property.

timeoutSeconds.description: How long to wait before giving up on this call, 30-1800 seconds (default 600). Values outside that range are clamped. Segmentation of a large dataset can take many minutes, so prefer the default over a short wait.

name: read_help_topic
description: Read NimbusImage documentation on a topic — how a feature works, or how the user can do something themselves in the UI. Call this before explaining a workflow you are unsure about. The available topic slugs are listed in the system prompt.

topic.description: The topic slug to read (e.g. "workflows", "image-processing"). Must be one of the slugs listed in the system prompt.

name: create_analysis_plot
description: Add a plot to the Analysis panel, optionally with a rectangular gate that filters the objects shown everywhere in the app. Plot two computed properties against each other (or a property against a categorical field like tags/channel). Supply xRange and/or yRange to gate — e.g. area 100-500 keeps only objects in that band, and the viewer, object list and exports all narrow to them. Gates chain: each plot narrows what the next one sees. Both axes must be properties to gate by range; for a categorical axis create the plot and let the user draw the gate. Prefer this over set_annotation_filter when the user is thinking in terms of a population on a scatter plot, or wants sequential gating. Visible immediately; reversible.

xAxis.description: One axis: either a computed property (propertyPath) or an annotation field (categorical). Exactly one of the two.

propertyPath.description: Property path as returned by get_property_values, e.g. ["<propertyId>", "Area"].

categorical.description: An annotation field to use as a category axis.

yAxis.description: One axis: either a computed property (propertyPath) or an annotation field (categorical). Exactly one of the two.

propertyPath.description: Property path as returned by get_property_values, e.g. ["<propertyId>", "Area"].

categorical.description: An annotation field to use as a category axis.

xRange.description: Inclusive-ish bound on this axis. Omit min or max for a one-sided gate. Providing xRange and/or yRange creates a rectangular gate.

yRange.description: Inclusive-ish bound on this axis. Omit min or max for a one-sided gate. Providing xRange and/or yRange creates a rectangular gate.

name: clear_analysis_plots
description: Remove every plot and gate from the Analysis panel, widening the object set back to whatever the ordinary filters allow. Use when the user wants to start a gating strategy over. Destructive and shared: the plots live in the dataset's configuration, so this discards gating work anyone on the dataset drew, and the polygons cannot be reconstructed. Requires the user's approval. If they are only asking why few objects are showing, read the gates with get_interface_state and explain them instead.
